body.statement: If \(c<C\), then uniformly over \(\mathcal M\), \(\mathbb E\|\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O((\log N)^{-1})\), \(\mathbb E d_H(\Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N,\preceq),\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq))=O((\log N)^{-1})\), and \(\mathbb E d_H(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq))=O((\log N)^{-1})\).
body.justification: The theorem quantifies both estimation loss and the excess size of an honest set.
body.gap: The logarithmic covariance rate is known from Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov; uniform expected Hausdorff control for the entire causal fiber is not stated there.
body.consumer: It supplies a rate for the minimum absolute compatible effect, a one-Lipschitz IDA ranking summary.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(d=|\mathcal R|\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\text{-}dimension}\) makes \(d=p(p+1)/2\) fixed as \(N\to\infty\).  For all sufficiently large \(N\), the definition \(\alpha_N=\min\{\alpha,(N+1)^{-2}\}\) gives \(\alpha_N=(N+1)^{-2}\).  The deterministic quantities in \(\mathrm{def:ray\text{-}region}\) then satisfy
\[
 t_N^2=\frac{\log N}{4\Lambda},
 \qquad
 m_N=c(1+t_N)^{-Q}N^{-1/4},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_N=2\sqrt{\frac{\log(4d/\alpha_N)}{N}}.
\tag{12}
\]
Because \(c>0\), \(Q<\infty\), and \(\Lambda<\infty\) are fixed class constants,
\[
 \frac{\varepsilon_N}{m_N}
 =\frac{2}{c}N^{-1/4}(1+t_N)^Q
   \sqrt{\log(4d/\alpha_N)}
 =O\!\left(N^{-1/4}(1+\sqrt{\log N})^Q\sqrt{\log N}\right)
 =o(1).
\tag{13}
\]
Here the last equality follows because every fixed power of \(\log N\) is \(o(N^{1/4})\).  Equations (12)--(13) imply that \(t_N\ge1\) and \(m_N\ge2\varepsilon_N\) for all sufficiently large \(N\); hence the active branch is eventually selected, deterministically and uniformly over \(P_X\in\mathcal M\).  Since \(c<C\), \(\log(C/c)>0\), and therefore
\[
 w_N
 =t_N^{-2}\left\{\log(C/c)+4\varepsilon_N/m_N\right\}
 =O((\log N)^{-1}),
 \qquad
 \Delta_N=\frac{3p}{2}w_N=O((\log N)^{-1}).
\tag{14}
\]
All constants in (13)--(14) depend only on the fixed declared class constants.

For such \(N\), let \(\mathcal E_N\) be the simultaneous Fourier event from \(\mathrm{thm:fourier\text{-}region}\).  On \(\mathcal E_N\), that theorem gives
\[
 \lVert\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le2\Delta_N.
\tag{15}
\]
It also gives, uniformly in \(P_X\in\mathcal M\),
\[
 P_X^N(\mathcal E_N^c)\le\alpha_N=(N+1)^{-2}.
\tag{16}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N^c\), both \(\widehat\Gamma_N\) and \(\Gamma\) have spectra in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\): this follows respectively from spectral clipping and the defining spectral restrictions of \(\mathcal M\).  In particular,
\[
 \lVert\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le \lVert\widehat\Gamma_N\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}+\lVert\Gamma\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le2\Lambda.
\tag{17}
\]
Splitting the expectation over \(\mathcal E_N\) and its complement and using (14)--(17) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P_X\in\mathcal M}
 \mathbb E_{P_X^N}\lVert\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le2\Delta_N+2\Lambda\alpha_N \\
 &=O((\log N)^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]

The deterministic inequality in \(\mathrm{lem:fiber\text{-}lipschitz}\) applies on every sample outcome because the two covariance matrices have spectra in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\).  Taking expectations in that inequality and applying (18) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P_X\in\mathcal M}
 \mathbb E_{P_X^N}d_H\!\left(
   \Theta_{TY}(\widehat\Gamma_N,\preceq),
   \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\right) \\
 &\qquad\le L_\beta
 \sup_{P_X\in\mathcal M}
 \mathbb E_{P_X^N}\lVert\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 =O((\log N)^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
The cited Lipschitz inequality explicitly includes collision points, so no effect-separation margin is used in (19).

For the confidence-set loss, \(\mathrm{thm:whole\text{-}fiber\text{-}coverage}\) gives on \(\mathcal E_N\) both
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\subseteq C_N
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{ex}\!\left(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\right)
 \le4L_\beta\Delta_N.
\]
The reverse directed excess is zero under the displayed inclusion, so
\[
 d_H\!\left(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\right)
 \le4L_\beta\Delta_N
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal E_N.
\tag{20}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N^c\), both sets are nonempty compact subsets of \([ -\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]\).  For the true fiber this follows from \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\) and the bound \(|\beta_J(\Gamma)|\le\Lambda/\lambda\), proved from the Schur-complement formula and the spectral bounds in \(\mathrm{thm:whole\text{-}fiber\text{-}coverage}\).  For \(C_N\) it follows from its clipping in \(\mathrm{def:fiber\text{-}region}\); nonemptiness follows because every center \(\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N)\) itself lies in that clipping interval.  Therefore
\[
 d_H\!\left(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\right)
 \le\frac{2\Lambda}{\lambda}
 \quad\text{on }\mathcal E_N^c.
\tag{21}
\]
Using (14), (16), and (20)--(21), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{P_X\in\mathcal M}
 \mathbb E_{P_X^N}d_H\!\left(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\right) \\
 &\qquad\le4L_\beta\Delta_N
   +\frac{2\Lambda}{\lambda}\alpha_N
 =O((\log N)^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{22}
\]
Equations (18), (19), and (22) are the three asserted uniform expectation bounds.  Since big-O assertions concern only sufficiently large \(N\), the finitely many values before the active branch begins do not affect the conclusion.
